newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's PMDB to vote on re-election - presidency.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's PMDB to vote on re-election - presidency.

text.p: Leaders of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) have agreed to follow the government's timetable in Congress for voting on re-election, a presidential spokesman said.

Despite a motion passed at a PMDB convention on Sunday, preventing the party's legislators from voting on re-election until February 15, party members will be free to vote ahead of that date on the issue, spokesman Sergio Amaral said.
"There was agreement that the motion voted yesterday was a recommendation and that it should not upset the timetable for voting on re-election," Amaral said.

The government intends to put a constitutional amendment allowing re-election to a vote in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies on Tuesday, followed on Wednesday by the first of two votes on the floor of the lower house.

"The re-election amendment will be voted in the committee and, according to the (PMDB Congressmen) who took part in the meeting, the timetable for the re-election amendment would be maintained," Amaral told reporters.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso demanded that the PMDB -- which has three ministers in his cabinet -- act more like an ally, the spokesman said.
"The PMDB cannot be in the government and behave as if it were in the opposition," Amaral said.

Amaral also said Cardoso would not tolerate any linking of the PMDB's support for re-election to elections for the presidencies of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate due in the first week of February.
The PMDB is the largest party in both houses of Congress and has generally voted in line with the government in the first two years of Cardoso's administration.

But the re-election issue has split the PMDB between those in favor and those against the government. Matters came to a head at Sunday's convention when the anti-Cardoso wing of the party won approval of recommendations that the party vote against the amendment, and only after February 15.
